name: LiveKit Server
description: Open-source WebRTC SFU / realtime media server that is the backbone for self-hosted realtime voice-AI agents (LiveKit Agents framework workers connect out to it). Exposes an HTTP/WebSocket signaling endpoint on port 7880 (RTC signaling at /rtc, room/management RPC via Twirp under /twirp/*), plus TCP 7881 and a UDP/ICE range for media. Room access requires a signed JWT minted with the server's API key/secret; the classic weakness is the well-known development key pair (devkey/secret) left in place.
auth_notes: LiveKit gates room join and all RoomService management RPCs behind a JWT signed with an API key + secret pair configured on the server; without a valid token the signaling endpoint rejects join and management calls. This makes the platform auth_tier B (token required) rather than fully open. The dominant real-world failure is credential defaults and leakage: running 'livekit-server --dev' (and countless copied livekit.yaml quickstarts) uses the published pair API key 'devkey' / secret 'secret', so anyone can forge admin-level tokens; API keys/secrets are also frequently committed to client bundles and repos. auto_create_room is enabled by default, so a valid (or forged-with-default-secret) token can spin up rooms freely. The HTTP endpoint itself (health, validate) answers unauthenticated and is the fingerprint surface.

shodan_dorks.rationale: The server's HTTP index / validate response and error bodies reference LiveKit; direct name match on the canonical signaling port
Hitting /rtc or a Twirp RoomService path without a token returns a LiveKit auth-error body ('missing authorization header'); high-signal for an exposed but token-gated LiveKit signaling endpoint
Twirp RPC error envelopes name the livekit RoomService/EgressService; conjunction with the livekit token on 7880 is high-precision for the management RPC surface
Server header / build info on the signaling port for version-targeted enumeration against known CVE-fixed releases

known_vulns: Default development credentials — 'livekit-server --dev' and copied quickstart livekit.yaml ship API key 'devkey' / secret 'secret'; an attacker who knows the pair forges admin JWTs and fully controls the server
API key/secret leakage — secrets embedded in client JS bundles or committed to repos allow token forgery (RoomService admin, egress, ingress, SIP)
Room enumeration and hijack — with a valid/forged token, ListRooms + ListParticipants + join expose live realtime voice/video sessions and let an attacker join or inject data
auto_create_room enabled by default — forged tokens can create arbitrary rooms and consume media/compute resources
Egress abuse — StartRoomCompositeEgress can record/exfiltrate live sessions to attacker-controlled storage when egress creds are reachable
SIP/Ingress abuse — CreateSIPTrunk / CreateIngress can bridge external telephony/streams into rooms, a toll-fraud and injection vector
Unauthenticated info surface — /rtc/validate and health endpoints disclose configuration/version details useful for CVE scoping without a token
risk_notes: LiveKit is token-gated, so an exposed :7880 is not automatically open — but the ecosystem's default 'devkey'/'secret' pair collapses that gate for a large fraction of self-hosted instances. Chain: (1) find :7880 with the LiveKit/twirp/missing-authorization signature -> (2) test the default key pair (or a secret harvested from the operator's client JS bundle / repo) -> (3) mint an admin JWT -> (4) ListRooms/ListParticipants to enumerate live realtime voice-AI sessions, join or inject data, start egress to record/exfiltrate audio+video, or abuse SIP/ingress for telephony bridging and toll fraud. Even without a working key, the unauthenticated /rtc/validate + error envelopes reliably fingerprint the server and leak version for CVE scoping. Note on scope: the LiveKit *Agents* framework (livekit/agents) is a worker library that dials OUT to this server and exposes no inbound port of its own — the exposed, fingerprintable surface is the LiveKit server documented here.
deployment_notes: Distributed as the livekit/livekit-server Docker image and Go binary; commonly self-hosted via docker-compose or Kubernetes behind a TLS-terminating LB. Ports: 7880/tcp = HTTP + WebSocket signaling (and RoomService Twirp RPC), 7881/tcp = TCP fallback for WebRTC media, 7882/udp (and a configurable UDP range, often 50000-60000) = ICE/RTP media; a Redis dependency backs multi-node clustering. Realtime voice-AI stacks run LiveKit Agents workers (Python/Node) that register outbound to the server and orchestrate STT->LLM->TTS pipelines inside rooms — so on the wire only the server's 7880 is the discoverable service. Internet exposure is normal and intended (clients must reach signaling), which makes the credential posture the whole security story: production requires operator-generated key/secret pairs, but --dev defaults and secret leakage are widespread. Not previously in the tome corpus.
